title: 1  Gannel ERM 2025-2026 analysis
section: 1.3 Organic matter per cubic metre of wet sediment
text:
1.3 Organic matter per cubic metre of wet sediment
We want to calculate the mass of organic matter per cubic metre of sediment. This is given by \[
\text{kg OM/m}^3 = \rho_{ws} \times p_{ds} \times p_{om}
\] where \(\rho_{ws}\) is the density of the wet sediment, \(p_{ds}\) is the proportion of dry sediment in the wet sediment and \(p_{om}\) is the proportion of organic matter in the dry sediment.
We will calculate eeach of these terms separately

title: 1  Gannel ERM 2025-2026 analysis
section: 1.4 Calculate proportions of water and dry sediment in the wet sediment
text:
1.4 Calculate proportions of water and dry sediment in the wet sediment

# proportion by mass of wet sediment that is dry sediment
gannel <- gannel |>
  mutate (p_ds = (sediment_cooked_inc_boat - boat_empty )/(boat_wet_sediment  - boat_empty ))


# proportion by mass of dry sediment that is organic matter
gannel <- gannel |>
  mutate (p_om = 1-  (crucible_ash - crucible_empty )/(crucible_sediment  - crucible_empty ))

title: 1  Gannel ERM 2025-2026 analysis
text:
1.5 Density of wet sediment
To calculate wet sediment density, we note:
\[
\begin{align}
\frac{1}{\rho_{ws}} &= \frac{p_{ds}}{\rho_{ds}} + \frac{p_w}{\rho_w}\\
&=\frac{p_{ds}\rho_{w} + p_w\rho_{ds}}{\rho_{ds}\rho_w}
\end{align}
\] Hence
\[
\begin{align}
\rho_{ws}=\frac{\rho_{ds}\rho_w}{p_{ds}\rho_{w} + p_w\rho_{ds}}
\end{align}
\] But \(p_w = 1-p_{ds}\) and \(\rho_w=1000\)kg/m3.
Hence \[
\begin{align}
\rho_{ws}=\frac{1000\rho_{ds}}{1000p_{ds} + (1-p_{ds})\rho_{ds}}
\end{align}
\] Check that this formula makes sense: what does it give as the density of the wet density if the proportion of dry sediment is either zero or one?
We see that we need the density of the dry sediment. We measured the quantities need to calculate this for our samples:

# density of dry sediment
gannel <- gannel |>
mutate(rho_ds = 1000* soil_mass/water_displacement)

We can now calcuate the density of wet sediment, given the density of dry sediment \(\rho_{ds}\) and the proportion \(p_{ds}\) of wet sediment that is dry sediment:

gannel <- gannel |>
  mutate(rho_ws = 1000*rho_ds / (1000*p_ds + (1-p_ds)*rho_ds))

Now that we have all the terms we require, we can calculate the mass of organic matter per cubic metre of wet sediment:

gannel <- gannel |>
  mutate(mass_om = rho_ws * p_ds * p_om)

The carbon content is about 0.58 times the organic matter content (citation needed), and the mass of carbon per hectare in tonnes is numerically 10 times the mass of carnon per cubic metre in kg. Hence

gannel <- gannel |>
  mutate(mass_c =0.58 * 10 * mass_om)

We can now find the means of each of the two values measured for each transect

carbon_summary <- gannel|>
  group_by(transect) |>
  summarise(mean_c_mass = mean(mass_c))

Now we plot it:

carbon_summary |>
  filter(transect<8) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = transect, y = mean_c_mass)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(x = "Transect", 
       y = "Soil carbon tonnes / hectare") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,700)) +
  theme_cowplot()








A linear regression:

c_model <-lm(mean_c_mass ~ transect, data = carbon_summary)
summary(c_model)
